tone_statements.citation: Li, Suqin. 2015. The Bai Language: A Musical Language with Typological Ablative Cases. Open Journal of Social Sciences 3(12): 183-189.
tone_statements.quote: Bai has seven to nine tones, and has a few sound and tone variations among the three subdivisions of dialects. These make the language a musical one.

tone_statements.citation: Wang, Feng. 2015. Variations of laryngeal features in Jianchuan Bai. Journal of Chinese Linguistics 43(1B): 434-452.
tone_statements.quote: The tonal system in Jianchuan Bai has attracted much attention for its complex combinations of pitch and phonation type. In this paper, based on EGG signals, three parameters, namely F0, Open Quotient (OQ) and Speed Quotient (SQ), are extracted to examine the tonal quality. It is found that there are two non-modal phonation types, Harsh and Pressed, and roughly four groups of pitch pattern (31/31/41; 33/433; 55/54; 35) in the eight tonal categories. One pair of tones can only be distinguished from each other by phonation type since their pitches are the same. As for other pairs, both pitch and phonation type may contribute to the distinction between them.
tone_statements.locator: author abstract (JCL 43(1B), 2015), as deposited in Crossref
tone_statements.n_tones: 8 tonal categories (4 pitch groups x modal/non-modal)

sources.citation: Li, Suqin. 2015. The Bai Language: A Musical Language with Typological Ablative Cases. Open Journal of Social Sciences 3(12): 183-189.
sources.quote: Bai has seven to nine tones, and has a few sound and tone variations among the three subdivisions of dialects. These make the language a musical one.
sources.note: Short morphology paper (weak, second-hand on inventory): states 'Bai has seven to nine tones' varying across the three dialect groups; sec. 2 gives Niujie forms with Chao tone letters (31, 33, 44 tense, 55 lax, 35, 42, 21) and sec. 2.4.2 'superasegmental inflective changes' lists derivational tone alternations (e.g. pronoun o31 -> ɯ55 for accusative; tɯ̃44 'win' vs tshɯ̃55 'lose'; ta55.. ta42 noun/verb 'load/carry'). Not an analysis of the tone system.

sources.locator: author abstract (JCL 43(1B), 2015), as deposited in Crossref
sources.note: EGG study (F0, open quotient, speed quotient) of the eight tonal categories of Jianchuan Bai: two non-modal phonation types (harsh, pressed) and roughly four pitch-pattern groups (31/31/41; 33/433; 55/54; 35); one tone pair is distinguished by phonation type alone, others by pitch and phonation together; non-modal phonation varies across speakers (harsh vs pressed for the same tone) and can change within a syllable; argues 'harsh voice' [mid-falling F0, -OQ, -SQ] is a better label than 'high-pitched voice'.

sources.note: Publisher/university summary: EGG-based (F0, OQ, SQ) study of phonation variation in the tones of four Bai dialects; Jianchuan Jinxing Bai has nasalised rhymes and 8 tones (4 level, 3 falling, 1 rising); Dali Meiba 8 tones (4 falling, 3 level, 1 rising); Xiangyun Chengbei 7; Yuanjiang Anren 7; tense/lax laryngeal contrast traced historically; tone realisation may be carried mainly by phonation or mainly by F0, speakers differ in strategy; concludes that Bai phonation variation is a tone-adaptation mechanism under contact.
